transcript_text:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood CSM); Alex Chen (Maven VP Eng), Reema Patel (Maven Head of Security), Tom Alvarez (Procurement), Lina Gomez (Legal)

Auto Summary: quick procurement + legal sync, a few security asks, confirm next steps to get MSA/DPA back for countersign, schedule deeper infra call.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 40-ish minutes, we'll try to walk through the outstanding MSA/DPA items, the SLA asks, and then Priya will run quickly through the private and dedicated options and what the onboarding looks like.
00:22 Alex: Yeah thanks, Jordan. We wanted to get alignment so our legal and procurement teams can proceed — Tom and Lina are on for approvals.
00:30 Tom: Hi all, yep, main things for procurement are 1) confirmed vendor contact and PO process, 2) pricing worksheet, and 3) any required certs.
00:45 Jordan: Cool. Priya, do you want to kick off with the hosting options?
00:50 Priya: Sure. So high level, Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem). For Maven's use case — primarily customer-facing personalization at low latency — we usually recommend starting on Dedicated if you need predictable throughput and isolation, otherwise Hosted for fast time to value.
01:15 Reema: Quick question, the Dedicated option — does it keep customer data separate at rest and in transit? We need KMS integration and per-customer key support.
01:24 Priya: Yes, Dedicated gives data isolation; we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and TLS in transit. For VPC/private we can also do control plane separation. I should note that our private offering can be fully customer-managed networking and optional on-prem for air-gapped cases.
01:40 Reema: Okay good. Lina: from legal side, biggest issue is the DPA retention windows and subprocessors list. We need clarity on where logs are stored and the ability to audit.
01:52 Jordan: Totally, we can provide our subprocessor list and SOC 2 report. Priya will drop the pen-test summary.
02:03 Priya: Yep, I'll share the latest SOC 2 Type II and the most recent penetration test summary — there are a couple of medium findings that we documented and remediated, I'll include the remediation notes.
02:15 Lina: Also, we need SSO / SAML support and RBAC to be enterprise-grade. Can users be assigned roles via SCIM?
02:24 Priya: Yes, SAML SSO is supported and we have SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC supports several roles out of the box and custom roles via API. There was a note earlier about audit logs retention — we keep audit logs for 90 days by default, but extended retention is an add-on.
02:45 Alex: 90 days is a bit low for us, finance and compliance may want one year. What's cost implication?
02:52 Jordan: Extended logging is an add-on, I can include pricing in the worksheet. For Dedicated, you also get longer log retention in certain tiers.
03:05 Tom: On SLAs — our legal wants a 99.9% uptime SLA for the inference endpoint and a latency SLO for p95 below 250ms for our typical prompt sizes. Is that something you offer?
03:18 Priya: We do SLA tiers. For hosted API public tier the SLA is lower; for Dedicated we can offer 99.9% uptime with an SLA credit structure. The p95 latency target depends on model and instance sizing; we need to calibrate with your workload — sequence length, tokens per request, expected QPS. We can run a benchmark.
03:39 Alex: We will provide a sample payload and QPS targets. The p95 <=250ms is important. If we need private deployment to meet that, we want to understand the tradeoffs on cost.
03:50 Priya: Understood. We'll include a benchmarking plan in the technical deep-dive and provide Dedicated sizing and cost tradeoffs. Often caching and batching help reduce cost while keeping p95 low.
04:05 Lina: Legal also flagged indemnity clauses and limitation of liability in the MSA; we have a standard template we send to vendors, any flexibility there?
04:15 Jordan: We're open to reasonable redlines; our starting position is standard, but we can review specific indemnity language. I'll send a redline-friendly version and propose discussion points.
04:28 Lina: Great. For data residency, we have EU customer sets that must stay in EU. Do you have region pinning?
04:36 Priya: Yes — smart routing and region pinning are supported. For Hosted we have EU regions; for Dedicated or Private we can ensure all inference and logs stay in EU regions, and with Private we can run on-prem too.
04:48 Reema: Regarding auditability, we want to perform an occasional vendor security assessment. Is a third-party assessment allowed or do you require an NDA?
04:57 Jordan: We have a vendor assessment process; for certain items we can provide SOC reports and allow a standard security review. For more invasive testing we typically have a pen-test authorization and scope. We'll coordinate with you.
05:12 Tom: Procurement timeline — if legal signs off within two weeks, we can onboard in early July. Any blockers?
05:20 Jordan: The main blocker is the MSA redlines and DPA approvals. Also if you require a Private deployment, that adds onboarding time — typically 4–6 weeks for Private vs 1–2 weeks for Hosted/Dedicated.
05:36 Alex: Okay, likely we'll aim for Dedicated initially. Pricing will probably need executive sign-off. Jordan, can you provide a committed capacity price and a non-committed burst price?
05:45 Jordan: Yes — I'll include both in the pricing worksheet. We'll show monthly reserved capacity pricing and per-token pricing for hosted burst.
05:53 Priya: One small technical note: our key serving and KV cache acceleration assume standard CUDA-backed GPUs; if you run in a private on-prem env with non-standard hardware we need to validate kernel support. There can be small perf differences.
06:10 Alex: Makes sense. If we go Dedicated that's likely on AWS in our VPC — can you integrate into our KMS with customer-managed keys?
06:18 Priya: Yes, customer-managed KMS in AWS is supported for Dedicated. For Private we can do a similar integration but may need specific network peering.
06:27 Lina: For the DPA, we need a guaranteed deletion pathway for customer PII on contract termination. How is data deletion handled?
06:36 Jordan: We have a data lifecycle spec — we can remove stored logs and cached artifacts on termination and provide a deletion certificate. We'll include the specifics in the DPA redline.
06:46 Reema: One more on encryption — do you support HSMs for key storage?
06:52 Priya: We integrate with most cloud KMS providers; HSM-backed keys via cloud KMS are supported. For Private, we can integrate with an on-prem HSM if required, but that's part of the implementation plan.
07:05 Tom: Procurement needs the contact who can sign the master. Is there a named accounts rep?
07:12 Jordan: I'm your AE and I'm the primary commercial contact; Evan (CSM) will own onboarding. For contracting and AM, we have a commercial agreements team as backup. I'll CC the signing contact when I send the docs.
07:24 Evan: I'll coordinate onboarding timeline and introduction to solution ops.
07:28 Alex: Great. Any competitive concerns? Our CTO mentioned Anthropic and Bedrock as options.
07:34 Jordan: Common comparison; we typically position on cost-performance and production tooling — rollout controls, caching, and observability are differentiators. We'll include a short competitor comp in the appendix of the pricing doc.
07:48 Lina: On SLAs again, can we get specifics for credit calculation and remedies? Our legal will want precise language.
07:56 Jordan: Yes, we'll attach standard SLA schedule showing uptime definitions, credit calculations per downtime minute, and exclusions. If you need bespoke SLA we can escalate.
08:08 Priya: For the benchmark plan, we'll need a sample dataset, average sequence length, and expected QPS. We'll then run a dedicated benchmark on the matching model family and provide p50/p95/p99 latency numbers and cost per 1M tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted.
08:26 Alex: I'll send sample payloads and a QPS profile by end of day tomorrow.
08:30 Tom: Procurement also needs vendor references and order of precedence for appendices. Do you have customer references with similar retail workloads?
08:40 Jordan: Yes, we can provide anonymized references; I'll include a couple of retail customers and a case study.
08:47 Lina: On subcontractors and subprocessors list, we need to see the full list — particularly any data processing in non-EU territories.
08:55 Priya: We'll include the subprocessors manifest and region mapping. Note that certain telemetry and monitoring data are processed by our monitoring partner, which is US-based. We can discuss contractual protections.
09:10 Alex: For pricing approvals, what's the typical commercial cadence? Are deals above X spend require SLA add-on approval?
09:18 Jordan: For large committed spends we engage our enterprise sales and legal earlier; I'll flag this as an enterprise opportunity. We'll also provide an initial PO template.
09:27 Reema: A technical item — does Redwood provide token-level cost reporting for each route so we can attribute costs per feature?
09:34 Priya: Yes, Redwood Console includes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model and tracing hooks for tracing inference. That's part of Redwood Optimize.
09:44 Alex: Helpful. Last question from my side — onboarding checklist and timeline if we sign MSA next week?
09:51 Evan: Onboarding checklist: legal sign -> billing set up -> SSO + SCIM -> Dedicated capacity provisioning -> benchmarking -> integration. Estimated time: Hosted 1–2 weeks, Dedicated 2–3 weeks, Private 4–6 weeks depending on network.
10:12 Tom: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
10:18 Jordan: Recap: I will send the MSA and DPA with suggested redlines by 2026-06-24; Priya will share SOC 2 and pen-test notes by 2026-06-23; pricing worksheet and Dedicated estimate by 2026-06-25; Alex will send sample payloads by 2026-06-22. We'll schedule the technical deep-dive for the week of 2026-06-29.
10:36 Lina: We'll review redlines internally and get back within a week.
10:40 Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email and post the docs in the shared folder.
10:45 Alex: Thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
